messages:
Matt: Ran an nsys capture on the canary with the new kernel_selector heuristic. Seeing a 2x spike in attention_kernel runtime for some requests :confused:
Sasha: ugh, do you have the trace id? which model/seq len?
Matt: trace=run-2026-03-17-17-21, model=llama-70b, seq=2048. The GPU timeline shows long gaps between the selector decision on CPU and kernel launch. NVTX ranges are sparse — I think we missed ranges around KV lookup + batch_split.
Liam: can you paste the perfetto link or upload the nsys export?
Matt: https://perfetto.dev/trace/viewer?run-2026-03-17-17-21 (uploaded). Quick grep of the nsys csv: 
```
kernel,avg_ms,count
attention_kernel,4.2,1200
kv_lookup_kernel,0.3,4800
other_kernel,0.1,6000
```
But wall time for some requests shows 8ms waiting between "cpu:select_kernel" and the first attention_kernel call.
Reza: if nvtx ranges are missing, correlating CPU decision -> GPU launch is annoying. We should add a compact per-request span id into NVTX (push with a short ascii tag) so trace search can filter by request. That was sparse but very useful in other runs.
Ben: agreed. Maybe use a two-level naming scheme: "req/<trace_id>" as parent, and then child ranges like "req/<id>/kv-lookup", "req/<id>/batch-split", "req/<id>/kernel-select", "req/<id>/kernel:attention". Keeps names searchable and groups them on the GPU timeline.
Sasha: love that. Implementation detail: nvtxRangePushA accepts a const char*. Be careful about allocations in hot paths. We should intern the strings in a small bounded LRU or format them on the stack with a short id.
Matt: sketch of a minimal change: 
```
// per-request span helper (hot path friendly)
char tag[32];
int n = snprintf(tag, sizeof(tag), "r:%u:k:%02u", req_id_short, span_kind);
nvtxRangePushA(tag);
// do work
nvtxRangePop();
```
This keeps strings <= 32 bytes, no heap alloc.
Liam: for span_kind we can use small enums: 1=kv,2=batch,3=select,4=kernel. That makes tags compact. Might also add a color code via nvtxRangePushEx with payload->color so the UI groups them.
Reza: note overhead — each NVTX push/pop is ~100-200ns on CPU. For very hot inner kernels we should avoid full per-token pushes. Keep micro-spans for coarse things: kv-lookup, batch-split, kernel-select. Don't annotate every layer. Also provide a build-time flag to enable verbose NVTX only in experiments.
Ben: another pain point: when we fallback to quantized kernel variants we lose consistent names. Suggest normalizing kernel labels in runtime mapping so the nvtx label is stable (e.g. "kernel:attention.fp16.q4" -> "kernel:attention" plus attribute payload for variant).
Sasha: how about the batching boundary? We currently have one "batch" nvtx range but we don't mark the split boundary (where inputs are separated into micro-batches). If we add "split" range we can see scheduling holes.
Matt: sample command I ran for others to reproduce: 
```
nsys profile -o run-2026-03-17-17-21 --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx
```
Upload is in the run folder.
perf-bot: Auto-capture attached: s3://redwood-nsys/run-2026-03-17-17-21.nsight and perfetto json. :robot_face:
Liam: next steps I propose:
- add compact per-request nvtx tag (r:<short>) for parent range
- emit coarse child spans: kv, batch-split, kernel-select, kernel-launch
- keep kernel nvtx label normalized and put variant as metadata (payload color / numeric id)
- gate verbose nvtx behind runtime flag and sampling mode
Sasha: +1. I'll take the nvtx helper change (low risk) and send a small PR with tests that verify no heap allocs in hotpath.
Reza: I'll add a perf test that runs microbench with and without NVTX to quantify overhead across seq lengths. If overhead >1% at scale we disable per-token spans by default.
Matt: thanks folks. If anyone captures an nsys with the tag we can iterate on naming. For immediate debugging I'll add a "req/shortid" parent span and a "kernel-select" child.
Ben: :thumbsup: ping me if you want me to normalize kernel names in the kernel registry.
Sasha: creating a tiny RFC doc in eng-runtime/notes after this thread so we have a reference for naming convnet.
Matt: cool. tagging this as follow-up for next perf sync. :eyes:
